reason: The methane store matches the lander's methane tank, so connecting it should fill one of the separate flight tanks.
expectation: I expect methane to transfer into its tank; the oxygen tank will still need filling.

alternatives.reason: The oxygen store also matches its tank and should advance the same goal; I chose methane first arbitrarily.

reaction: The rising cockpit indicator makes the progress toward departure feel tangible.
reason: The oxygen store matches the remaining flight tank, and this is the only available combination.
expectation: I expect liquid oxygen to transfer into its separate tank and complete the goal.

effect: The oxygen transfer completed the separate flight tanks and clarified that fuel and oxidizer meet in the engine, while their storage and connections remain separate.
reaction: The distinction between separate storage and meeting in the engine was a useful detail.

mostWorthwhile.text: Filling the oxygen tank was most worthwhile because its explanation made the different roles of fuel and oxidizer clearer.

leastWorthwhile.text: The two transfers were straightforward and similarly structured, so the chapter offered little room for a meaningful decision.

surprise.text: The explanation that the two liquids meet in the engine clarified why they remain separate in storage.

arbitrary.text: Choosing methane first was arbitrary; both matching transfers were available and had an evident purpose.

continue.text: I would continue to see how the specimens and their surrounding ice make it home, although this chapter's combinations were predictable.
